cards.text: It's the Sabbath, the seventh day God set apart for rest (Exodus 20:8-10). Jesus is passing through the grainfields with His disciples, and they start picking the heads of grain as they go. Friend, you KNOW somebody's about to have something to say about that.

cards.question: Walking through the grainfields on the Sabbath, the disciples pick the heads of grain, ___ them in their hands, and eat them.

cards.text: And somebody does. Some of the Pharisees, the strictest group in their religion (Acts 26:5), have a QUESTION, and it is not a friendly one.

cards.question: Some Pharisees see the disciples picking and eating grain on the Sabbath. What's their complaint?

answers.text: They say it is unlawful on the Sabbath
They say the field belongs to someone else
They say the disciples should have washed first

cards.text: Jesus answers with a question of His own: have they not read what David, Israel's famous king, did when he and his companions were hungry? Asking the Pharisees if they've read the Scriptures is like asking me if I've ever HEARD of an oven.

cards.question: In the story Jesus brings up, David and his hungry companions go into the house of God.
Inside the house of God, David takes the consecrated ___ and gives it to his companions.
David ate the consecrated bread from the house of God and shared it. By law, who was allowed to eat it?

cards.text: Then Jesus makes a declaration. Friend, you're gonna want to sit DOWN for this one.

cards.question: Jesus makes a declaration to the Pharisees in the grainfields. What does He say the Son of Man is?

cards.text: On another Sabbath, Jesus goes into the synagogue and teaches. A man is there whose right hand is withered.

The scribes and Pharisees are there too, watching Jesus closely and looking for a reason to accuse Him. It's like a coworker standing behind your desk all day, just WAITING for you to open the wrong tab.

cards.question: In the synagogue, the scribes and Pharisees are watching Jesus closely. What are they waiting to see?

answers.text: If He will heal on the Sabbath
If He will read from the scroll
If He will leave the synagogue early

cards.text: But Jesus knows their thoughts. I bet they think they're being sneaky, but that's like planning a surprise party in a group chat the guest of honor is IN.

cards.question: Jesus knows what the scribes and Pharisees are thinking. What does He tell the man with the withered hand?

answers.text: Get up and stand among us

cards.text: So the man gets up and stands right there in front of everybody. Then Jesus puts a question to them.

cards.question: In the synagogue, Jesus asks which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do ___, to save life or to ___ it?

cards.text: Jesus looks around at all of them. Then He turns to the man with one instruction.

cards.question: Jesus looks around at everyone in the synagogue, then speaks to the man with the withered hand. What does He tell him?

answers.text: Show your hand to the priest

cards.question: The man with the withered hand is too afraid to stretch it out in front of the scribes and Pharisees.

cards.text: He does it, and his hand is restored. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer with my edges worn down to NOTHING, so trust me, I know a made-new moment when I see one.

cards.question: After Jesus heals the man's hand on the Sabbath, the scribes and Pharisees are filled with ___.
After the healing, the scribes and Pharisees begin to discuss with one another what they might do to Jesus.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "hold" is a near-match. The disciples are holding the grain in their hands while they rub it (Luke 6:1), so a baker could argue that "hold them in their hands" is true. Replace it with an answer that is clearly false.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The statement marked True says David and his companions go into the house of God. Luke 6:4 says only that "He entered the house of God" and then gave the bread to his companions. The text never says the companions went in, and it doesn't clearly imply it either. The statement should be about David entering.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: This is the first time the scribes appear (Luke 6:7), and the card doesn't say who they are. The Pharisees got a short introduction in stop 1, card 3, but the scribes get none.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
